meta.title: Theory of Change — Open Energy Transition
meta.description: How Open Energy Transition drives global impact: transparent, accessible, collaborative and adoptable energy planning with open-source models and data.

hero.title:
Our Theory of Change:
Driving Global Impact
lead: At Open Energy Transition (OET), we transform global energy planning by promoting the use of open-source models and data.
Our focus is on creating a global impact through promoting transparency, flexibility, accessibility, and collaboration in energy planning.

challenge.label: The Challenge
challenge.statement: Traditional 'black-box' modelling approach in energy planning lacks transparency and
challenge.emphasis: slows down the global energy transition.
details: Furthermore, there are challenges in getting open-source tools adopted
in companies due to the lack of support and software requirement gaps.

goal.label: Our Goal
goal.statement: Is to address these challenges and accelerate the global energy transition.
details: We aim to make energy planning more transparent, accessible, and collaborative
and to make open-source tools more adoptable for companies, thus driving a global impact.

steps.title: Facilitate Standardization of Open Data
steps.text: We promote the creation and use of robust, open datasets that can be used in energy system models.

steps.title: Advance Open-Source Planning Tools
steps.text: We facilitate technical advancements in OS tools and support development of enterprise-grade tools to software maturity.

steps.title:
Provide Reliable
Support
steps.text: We offer reliable support for the use, scalability and security of the open planning solution to increase utility and trust for users.

steps.title: Build Credibility & Regulatory Support
steps.text: We build credibility and regulatory support for OS grid planning tools and scale the adoption for industry and regulatory decisions.

steps.title: Expand User & Developer Community
steps.text: Bolster the pool of analytical talent to collaboratively improve tools, expand the base of users who can integrate and apply these tools.

columns.description: Increased number of studies using open data and increased open data quality.
columns.outcome: More robust and sustainable energy systems.

columns.description: Increased number of users and downloads of the open-source tools.
columns.outcome: Increased public acceptance of energy infrastructure upgrades.

columns.description: Increased number of companies and institutions adopting open-source tools for energy planning.
columns.outcome: Lower costs of the whole energy infrastructure.

columns.description: Increased number of energy planning studies created using the open-source tools.
columns.outcome: Increased adoption of inclusive open-source tools.

impact.title: Impact
impact.text: Ultimately, our work will lead to more companies around the world adopting open-source tools for energy planning. This is how we aim to create a global impact.
